scope: OpenWrt 秒 Pin: make the reaver speed flags unconditional and stop abandoning a slow candidate after a fixed 60 seconds.
background: Compared two community 秒 PIN shell scripts (crack_wps_2025-0907.sh, reaver_v5-2.sh) with the in-app quick WPS flow. The scripts run reaver -S -N -d0 -t5 and wait for an explicit reaver outcome instead of a fixed per-candidate deadline.
findings: The app previously carried -S -N only through the default additional_args value '-S -N -l 30'. A user who cleared or replaced that field silently lost the speed flags, so they were not guaranteed.
The quick flow defaulted to 60 seconds per candidate and the quick dialog offered 0 = unlimited, but most saved profiles kept 60.
The system WPS sender already treats 0 as one bounded registration attempt (120 seconds), so the new default does not make that path unbounded.
changes: reaver base command now always includes -S (small DH) and -N (no NACK); -S/-N tokens in additional_args are ignored so the command never duplicates them.
quick_seconds default is now 0 (no per-candidate time cap); the settings, dialogs, diagnostics and remembered-PIN path all use the same default.
One-time settings migration: an existing profile without wps_quick_defaults_version and with quick_seconds == 60 is moved to 0; after the marker is written, a user-chosen 60 is preserved.
Quick WPS dialog and advanced tooltips now state the unlimited default and the fixed -S/-N behavior.

files.finding: with NACK sending disabled the receive timer is started manually, so the comment about waiting 'infinitely' is explicitly mitigated
pixie passes -S to pixiewps when small DH is enabled, so the flags stay consistent in offline mode

pixiewps.finding: -S/--dh-small means private key = 1 and public key = 2; pixiewps exploits this and stays compatible with the reaver small-DH mode

tests.command: python -m unittest tests.test_wps_* (all 17 wps test modules)
new_coverage: quick default keeps max_runtime 0 (no per-candidate cap)
online and offline quick commands contain -S and -N
additional_args -S -N are ignored without duplicating the flags; other forbidden tokens still raise
explicit quick_seconds still produces a finite max_runtime
legacy quick_seconds 60 migrates to 0 exactly once, and a later explicit 60 is kept
tests.ui_check: Quick WPS dialog rendered offscreen in light and dark themes; description, unlimited value and button row show no clipping or overlap

limitations: No live router comparison against the community scripts; speed gain and lock behavior are unverified on real hardware.
Default remains 1 second attempt delay (-d) and -l 30; the scripts use -d0 -l61. Changing these defaults was not requested and could increase WPS lock risk.
Hardlinks and special archive entries are unrelated to this change and remain rejected by the backup path.
